title: Trace Sink Selection Middleware for Multi-Vendor Tracing Backends
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Build a lightweight middleware component that routes incoming tracing envelopes to an appropriate downstream tracing backend (Tempo, Jaeger, external vendor endpoints) based on tenant policy and payload attributes. Goals: 1) enable per-tenant sink binding without forcing dual-writes across all customers, 2) perform minimal format normalization (trace id/span id, attributes mapping, timestamp correction) to satisfy backend schemas, 3) provide resilient delivery with backoff, durable buffering, and a configurable fallback policy, and 4) surface routing decisions to the Console and SLO dashboards for debugging and alerts. This component sits between our OTLP ingress and existing export pipeline and must be compatible with current sampling/aggregation hooks. It should be testable in isolation (local dev harness) and include feature flags for canary rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Middleware can inspect incoming OTLP/Zipkin envelopes and select a target sink per tenant according to policy mapping
Tracing envelopes are translated where necessary (minimal tag/key remapping) and validated against downstream schema before send
Backpressure/backoff path buffers to persistent queue with metrics and retry windows configurable per-tenant
Canary rollout path exists (console toggle + header override) and default fallback is to store-and-forward to S3 for later replay
End-to-end integration tests against mocked Tempo and Jaeger sinks with golden-trace comparison pass in CI
Console exposes a Trace Routing drilldown: recent routing decisions, error rate per sink, queued envelope count, and last-failure reasons
